sourcedFrom: 940™ AUTO-LOADING SHOTGUN — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 104871 ("940 Autoloading Owners Manual2"), typeset 10/29/21 (2021 (typesetting stamp 10/29/21 on every page; no separate copyright line is printed))
cleanIntro: The 940's whole reputation rests on its gas system staying clean, and Mossberg's own interval says so — thorough cleaning every 500 rounds. Empty the magazine tube before the chamber, get the barrel off by whichever of the three front-end arrangements your gun has, strip the gas stack off the tube, then the action out the front and the trigger housing down on its two pins.

steps.title: Safety ON, and your fingers off the trigger for the whole unload
steps.action: Set the safety fully rearward to ON and keep the muzzle pointed somewhere harmless. Unloading a 940 means running the action and releasing shells under spring pressure, so the trigger is the one part your hands stay away from until the gun is proven empty.
steps.quote: Set the safety button fully rearward to the “ON” (SAFE) position. During unloading, never allow your fingers or any other object to contact the trigger.
steps.cite: 940™ AUTO-LOADING SHOTGUN — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 104871 ("940 Autoloading Owners Manual2"), typeset 10/29/21 — UNLOADING THE FIREARM, p.19

steps.title: Magazine tube first, trigger guard up, one shell at a time
steps.action: Turn the gun so the trigger guard faces up, hold the elevator down with your thumb and press the bolt release. One shell comes off the tube each time, driven by the magazine spring — catch them rather than letting them fall. Repeat until nothing more comes out.
steps.aside: This will release one shotshell from the magazine tube under spring pressure.
steps.quote: First, remove the shotshells from the magazine tube.
steps.cite: 940™ AUTO-LOADING SHOTGUN — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 104871 ("940 Autoloading Owners Manual2"), typeset 10/29/21 — UNLOADING THE FIREARM, p.19

steps.title: Then the chamber, and lock the action open
steps.action: With the tube empty, pull the operating handle fully rearward: that ejects whatever was chambered and locks the bolt back. Doing this before the tube is empty just chambers the next shell, which is exactly the mistake the order is written to prevent.
steps.quote: With the magazine tube empty, pull the operating handle fully rearward.
steps.cite: 940™ AUTO-LOADING SHOTGUN — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 104871 ("940 Autoloading Owners Manual2"), typeset 10/29/21 — UNLOADING THE FIREARM, p.19

steps.title: Prove all three places empty, then glasses on
steps.action: Look at and put a finger into the chamber, the elevator and the magazine tube. Then put eye protection on before anything else moves — the magazine spring and the gas system return spring are both compressed on that tube, and a magazine extension is holding one of them in.
steps.aside: Wear eye protection during disassembly and cleaning to protect your eyes from oil spatter or spring loaded components.
steps.quote: Lock the action open, visually and physically check the chamber, elevator, and magazine tube to ensure the firearm is completely unloaded
steps.cite: 940™ AUTO-LOADING SHOTGUN — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 104871 ("940 Autoloading Owners Manual2"), typeset 10/29/21 — DISASSEMBLY, p.19

steps.title: Find your front end first — extension and nut, +3, or plain cap
steps.action: Look at the muzzle end before you turn anything. A 940 leaves the factory in three arrangements — a magazine extension retained by a magazine nut, a +3 extension, or a plain magazine end cap — and the book gives each its own procedure. Working the wrong one is how people take a spring-loaded extension off believing it is a bare cap.
steps.quote: The action assembly of your model 940™ may be fitted with a magazine extension and a magazine nut.
steps.cite: 940™ AUTO-LOADING SHOTGUN — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 104871 ("940 Autoloading Owners Manual2"), typeset 10/29/21 — BARREL REMOVAL, p.20

steps.title: Palm over the cap — the magazine spring is under real pressure
steps.action: If yours has an extension or an end cap over the spring, keep your palm flat over it and unscrew slowly with light pressure. The spring runs the length of the tube and will come to full length the moment the retainer clears — let go and it goes across the room with the follower behind it.
steps.aside: The magazine spring will extend to its full length when the magazine end cap is removed.
steps.quote: CAUTION: The magazine spring is under considerable pressure and is retained by the magazine end cap.
steps.cite: 940™ AUTO-LOADING SHOTGUN — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 104871 ("940 Autoloading Owners Manual2"), typeset 10/29/21 — BARREL REMOVAL, p.20

steps.title: Barrel clamp and extension off, if fitted
steps.action: A 5/32" allen key takes the two barrel clamp screws, one per side. Then back the magazine extension off two turns only and unscrew the magazine nut with the extension still on it — Mossberg's instruction is not to take the extension off the nut completely, because separating them just gives you two loose parts and a spring you are no longer controlling.
steps.quote: Unscrew the magazine extension two turns.
steps.cite: 940™ AUTO-LOADING SHOTGUN — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 104871 ("940 Autoloading Owners Manual2"), typeset 10/29/21 — BARREL REMOVAL, p.20

steps.title: Forearm forward, barrel forward — the piston stays in the barrel
steps.action: Slide the forearm assembly forward and draw the barrel straight off the receiver and magazine tube. The gas piston is meant to stay in the gas cylinder portion of the barrel as it goes; if it walks back onto the tube, the barrel binds and people pull harder instead of looking.
steps.quote: Pull the barrel forward, free of the receiver and magazine tube.
steps.cite: 940™ AUTO-LOADING SHOTGUN — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 104871 ("940 Autoloading Owners Manual2"), typeset 10/29/21 — BARREL REMOVAL, p.20

steps.title: Catch the follower — it comes out of the tube on its own
steps.action: Point the magazine tube down and catch the follower as it drops. Note which way round it sits before it leaves your hand; a follower put back reversed will bind in the tube and mimic a feed problem you will then chase in the wrong place.
steps.quote: Note the proper orientation of the magazine follower for reassembly.
steps.cite: 940™ AUTO-LOADING SHOTGUN — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 104871 ("940 Autoloading Owners Manual2"), typeset 10/29/21 — BARREL REMOVAL, p.21

steps.title: Gas stack off the magazine tube in order
steps.action: Take the gas piston assembly out of the gas cylinder, then slide the spacer tube, pusher assembly, return spring and forearm retainer off the magazine tube. Lay them out in the order they came off — this stack goes back the same way and there is no keyway to save you.
steps.quote: Remove the gas piston assembly from the gas cylinder. Remove the spacer tube, pusher assembly, gas system return spring, and forearm retainer from the magazine tube (Figure 10).
steps.cite: 940™ AUTO-LOADING SHOTGUN — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 104871 ("940 Autoloading Owners Manual2"), typeset 10/29/21 — GAS SYSTEM COMPONENT REMOVAL, p.22

steps.title: Outer piston rings off — the inner one stays put
steps.action: The outer ring pries off with a small flat screwdriver next to its split; a two-ring piston has a retaining ring to come off first. The inner ring is factory-fitted and stays on the piston — removing it is not part of cleaning, and after cleaning it should still rotate freely.
steps.aside: This inner ring should not be removed during disassembly or cleaning.
steps.quote: The gas piston assembly has an inner piston ring installed by the factory.
steps.cite: 940™ AUTO-LOADING SHOTGUN — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 104871 ("940 Autoloading Owners Manual2"), typeset 10/29/21 — GAS PISTON DISASSEMBLY, p.22

steps.title: Trigger housing down on its two pins — and never open the housing
steps.action: Ride the bolt forward under control with the operating handle and the bolt release, then drift the two trigger housing retaining pins out of the receiver and pull the housing straight out. The pins will go either way. The housing itself does not come apart — Mossberg is explicit about it, and it is full of small sprung parts that do not go back by feel.
steps.aside: The trigger housing assembly is a complex assembly and must not be disassembled.
steps.quote: (The pins can be pushed out from either direction).
steps.cite: 940™ AUTO-LOADING SHOTGUN — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 104871 ("940 Autoloading Owners Manual2"), typeset 10/29/21 — TRIGGER HOUSING REMOVAL, p.23

steps.title: Nothing touches the trigger while the housing is out
steps.action: With the housing out of the receiver, leave the trigger alone. Letting the hammer fall with nothing supporting it batters the assembly and can catch a finger — this is the single most common bench injury on a shotgun trigger group.
steps.quote: Never pull the trigger while the trigger housing assembly is removed from the receiver, as personal injury or damage to the trigger housing assembly may result.
steps.cite: 940™ AUTO-LOADING SHOTGUN — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 104871 ("940 Autoloading Owners Manual2"), typeset 10/29/21 — TRIGGER HOUSING REMOVAL, p.24

steps.title: Operating handle out, action forward through the barrel opening
steps.action: Pull the operating handle straight out of the bolt, then press the bolt release and bring the bolt and slide forward out of the receiver through the barrel opening. Bolt lifts off the slide. Watch the link pin — it is a loose fit and drops free without warning.
steps.aside: The link pin in the action assembly is a loose fitting part and may fall free during removal/disassembly of the action. Proceed with caution.
steps.quote: Pull the operating handle straight out of the bolt (Figure 13).
steps.cite: 940™ AUTO-LOADING SHOTGUN — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 104871 ("940 Autoloading Owners Manual2"), typeset 10/29/21 — ACTION REMOVAL/DISASSEMBLY, p.24

steps.title: Field strip complete — Mossberg stops here
steps.action: Barrel, gas stack, piston rings, trigger housing, bolt and slide. That is the published teardown in full and the book closes it in the next sentence. Everything past this point is a gunsmith or the Product Service Center, and going further voids the warranty by Mossberg's own words.
steps.quote: Field disassembly is now complete. Further disassembly should only be performed by a qualified gunsmith or the Product Service Center.
steps.cite: 940™ AUTO-LOADING SHOTGUN — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 104871 ("940 Autoloading Owners Manual2"), typeset 10/29/21 — ACTION REMOVAL/DISASSEMBLY, p.24

deepAbsentReason: The 940 book publishes exactly one teardown and it ends where the steps above end. Its own closing line is "Field disassembly is now complete. Further disassembly should only be performed by a qualified gunsmith or the Product Service Center.", and it separately forbids opening the trigger housing and removing the inner piston ring. Everything Mossberg publishes past the field strip is a stock-fitting, sight-mounting or choke procedure, not a deeper strip, so there is no deep-clean content to author and the absence is recorded rather than filled.

cleaning.name: GAS SYSTEM — thorough, every 500 rounds
tasks: Stiff brass brush and solvent on the gas piston, magazine tube and gas cylinder
Inside AND outside of the outer gas rings — deposits here stop it cycling
Clean the cylinder bore so the piston travels its full range freely
Rag and solvent on the forearm retainer, spacer tube, pusher and return spring
Check the inner piston ring still rotates freely after cleaning
Light oil then wipe dry — excess oil accelerates carbon build-up

cleaning.name: BARREL & CHAMBER
tasks: Scrub bore and chamber with solvent and patch until clean
Keep a choke tube installed while cleaning the barrel so the threads stay clear
Leave no patch, oil or grease in the bore

cleaning.name: ACTION
tasks: Solvent on the bolt, slide and link to shift accumulated residue
Lubricate sparingly — they stay cleaner longer that way

cleaning.name: RECEIVER
tasks: Rag or soft bristle brush inside, working the bolt and slide tracks
A few drops of light oil in the tracks once clean
Never a metal-bristle brush on the receiver

cleaning.name: TRIGGER HOUSING
tasks: Soft bristle brush only, to shift loose residue
Housing stays closed; trigger stays untouched while it is out of the gun

reassembly: Safety ON. Bolt assembly on top of the slide, sitting flat.
Bolt and slide into the FRONT of the receiver, link first, wiggling side to side to engage the tracks; the bolt stops nearly flush with the front of the receiver.
Align the end of the link with the return spring plunger and press the bolt release — the link end MUST be in the plunger — then push the bolt back until the operating handle slot is fully visible.
Operating handle through the bolt into the slide, notch facing rearward, pushed in until the internal plunger engages; tug it outward to prove it is caught.
Trigger housing into the receiver, holes aligned, both pins pushed home.
Gas piston assembly back into the gas cylinder portion of the barrel, then forearm retainer, return spring, pusher assembly and spacer tube onto the magazine tube.
⛔ Confirm the gas piston is in the barrel's gas cylinder BEFORE the barrel goes on — Mossberg states this as a must, and a barrel fitted without it is a dangerous malfunction waiting to happen.
Barrel into the receiver, gas cylinder sliding over the magazine tube, pushed until fully seated; if it binds, pull the spacer tube back toward the receiver.
Forearm assembly on, then the magazine nut and extension (or the end cap) tightened hand tight only; barrel clamp halves and their two 5/32" screws last, not over-tight.
fncheck: Prove it empty, then pull the bolt fully rearward — it should lock open — and press the bolt release with fingers clear of the ejection port so it runs forward and locks closed. Repeat several times to feel the action run free. Then, action closed and safety ON, pull the trigger: the hammer must not fall. Finger off, safety to OFF: still no fall. Safety OFF and trigger pulled: the hammer should fall. Any other behaviour and it goes to the Product Service Center instead of the range.
